incident-bot: [PAGE] P1 - Dedicated pool pressure for fenwick-corp (vpc-tenant). GPU queueing >95% for 12m. Error rate 5% on /v1/generate. Paging oncall: maya

maya: oncall here, joining now. where are we seeing the spike?

liam: metrics: queue depth 820 -> 1200, p95 latency 720ms -> 2300ms, 504s from worker timeouts. No host OOMs reported yet.

arjun: this is a single-tenant dedicated pool (reserved capacity). autoscale is disabled by default for fenwick. We have two quick levers: 1) enable controlled burst to shared/ephemeral pool (takes ~30-60s to flip + extra cold-starts), 2) evict low-priority batch jobs in the pool to free memory. Spinning ephemeral nodes for capacity ~6-8m to be fully ready.

sarah: FYI CS said Fenwick kicked off large embedding + nightly report runs after a recent data refresh. They've agreed to pause non-critical jobs if we ask. Jordan is on the call with their infra lead.

jordan: confirmed — Fenwick accepts a short pause for heavy reports. They rely on inference for live product traffic though; we should avoid total capacity loss.

oliver: customer impact? SLA? any need to escalate to account team?

maya: impact: live API 5% errors, throughput reduction on some routes. SLA breach risk if sustained >30m.

liam: proposed mitigation plan: enable controlled burst (policy: token-rate cap 200k tokens/min for burst) + temporary rate-limiter on fenwick non-critical routes. Then evict lower-priority batch jobs. If burst insufficient, spin ephemeral nodes. Approve?

arjun: technical notes: to evict we can run `rctl drain --tenant fenwick --priority low` (instant). To patch concurrency: `rctl set-concurrency fenwick 6` (current 8) to reduce mem usage; safe but may increase request queuing a bit.

maya: are there risks to other tenants if we burst?

liam: risk: shared pool cold-start latency; minor increased p99 for unrelated tenants if we misconfigure rate limits. We'll set hard caps and isolation on ephemeral pool.

oliver: decision path: minimize customer impact quickly. If Fenwick agreed to pause, prefer evict + concurrency patch first, then burst if needed. Need a communication note to Fenwick.

jordan: messaging ready. I'll tell them: "we're freeing capacity and may briefly route some requests to an ephemeral pool; you might see slight p99 changes for <10m." They approve.

maya: action items: liam enable eviction/burst gating, arjun apply concurrency patch, jordan notify customer, sarah create incident ticket for postmortem.

liam: executing now: `rctl drain --tenant fenwick --priority low`

liam: drain started — evicted 42 low-priority tasks, queue depth dropping.

arjun: applying concurrency patch: `rctl set-concurrency fenwick 6` -> applied. Workers restarting gracefully.

incident-bot: mitigation update: queue depth falling to 430, error rate down to 1.2%, p95 latency 980ms.

maya: still watching. liam, if queue stabilizes under 500 for next 5m we hold. If it climbs again, enable burst.

liam: monitoring. if we need burst command: `redwood infra burst enable --tenant fenwick --pool ephemeral --token-rate 200000` (requires ops confirm).

jordan: Fenwick confirmed pause and appreciates quick response. They asked for ETA to full recovery.

arjun: estimate: with current drain+concurrency change we should be stable in 10-15m. If not, burst + ephemeral nodes add another ~8 minutes.

maya: agreed. I'll stay on call for 30m and then handoff to oncall rotation if stable. Please log actions in incident ticket.

liam: noting: burst not enabled. no cross-tenant impact observed. continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: [STATUS] mitigation in progress — metrics improving. Next auto-check at +5m.

maya: thanks team. will update after 30m. we'll schedule a short postmortem with fenwick to cover why batch jobs overlapped with peak live traffic and propose scheduling guardrails.

liam: I'll add temporary guardrail rule: block large embedding jobs during fenwick business hours for 24h while they adjust.

jordan: customer will await postmortem. they're ok for a follow-up call.

maya: handing off monitoring in 30m if stable. filing incident ticket with runbook and timeline.

liam: final note: no SLA hit yet. continue to watch.

maya: (end)
